requirement: Execute external commands safely using argument vectors without shell=True, preventing arbitrary command injection while enforcing allowlists, timeouts, and error handling.
skeleton: SafeCommandRunner class with run method and execute_command helper.

rationale.teaches: Command execution with an argument vector and shell=False, a non-empty string-list check, an allowlist that blocks anything not in it, and a positive timeout.
rationale.why: shell=True with a joined string runs every test command correctly and only fails when an argument contains a shell metacharacter. The fixture passes an argument with a semicolon and checks that it reaches the program literally.

candidates.why_wrong: Arguments are joined into a string and run with shell=True, so a semicolon in an argument executes a second command.
args is not validated, so a bare string is accepted and Popen splits it character by character.
A timeout of exactly 0 is accepted and every command expires immediately.
The allowlist check is inverted, so allowed commands are refused and any other command runs.
shell=True is passed with a list, so only the first element runs and the rest become shell positional parameters.
